Labor and food cost is significant in restaurants but it's not as high as you are making it out to be. Restaurants try to keep labor cost down not because it is so high but because every little expense eats into profits. I work with restaurant data and I can tell you food price markup outstrips labor and food costs by a significant amount. Of course the restaurant managers/owners will always complain about labor costs but that's more of a normal human bias against workers rather than the cause for their profit woes. They'll tell you otherwise but the numbers don't tell the same story.

Margin, markup and burden have nothing to do with food cost. It is a given that a larger high end restaurant can demand higher margins and has a higher burden, based on facilities and equipment, is going to charge the customer more. That's why the smaller "hole in the wall" guy can sell a taco at a lower price.

The data I see says that despite the burden most well run restaurants of all types (fast food, fast casual, full service or fine dining) can deliver strong profits. They would go out of business otherwise. I don't think OP was talking about fine dining mexican food restaurants so burden is likely less of an issue for them.
Rent/utilities and insurance are likely higher than labor wages monthly.

It's probably a number of reasons why the prices are going up. Outside of price increases due to all restaurants raising prices because the market will bear it, the biggest reason I think is the general demand all around for foodstuffs like fajita meat. Years ago when fajitas were hardly known outside of largely hispanic regions they were cheap to buy. It was considered a tough and lower quality cut of meat compared to steaks and roasts so demand was low. Now that everyone eats them they command higher prices. It's just like with chicken wings. Large packs of raw chicken wings used to sell for just a few bucks before the popularity of wings went up sharply. Now I can't find a package of raw chicken wings for less than chicken breasts. Large food makers are buying up these foods and reducing availability and lots of the products are being exported too further reducing availability. We keep paying these high prices and keep voraciously eating the food so prices will always go up in these cases. And just to confound things further, plain old greed and profit taking will figure in there too so we're screwed on prices no matter what. Mexican restaurants are just keeping pace with every other restaurant, including fast food who have raised prices dramatically over the last 10 years.
